term: temporal everlasting presence in one supplied history
definition: EverlastingAt h w x means IsAt w x t for every supplied time t, fixing one world and one individual. The control Time is Int with its full standard two-sided order, so the interpretation assigns presence throughout an unbounded past and future. This is not quantification over all accessible worlds, proof of modal necessity, or timeless Eternal. A History supplies now : Time and therefore witnesses inhabited time, but the generic predicate imposes no temporal order or unboundedness; the concrete Int control fixes that interpretation.
note: A precise temporal-presence role, distinguished from the sourced timeless eternity predicate. It models presence at temporal indices, not physical change or a metaphysical account of time. A designated time is required by History, while two-sided unboundedness is supplied by the concrete Int interpretation.
